page: Amazon Web Services m8i.24xlarge is a general-purpose instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture with an Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor, providing 96 vCPUs across 48 physical cores with 2.0 threads per core. The dedicated CPU operates at 3.9 GHz and includes a 480 MB L3 cache. It is equipped with 384.0 GB of DDR5 memory running at 7 GHz, yielding 4.0 GB of memory per core. The instance does not include local storage or GPUs, and it provides a baseline network bandwidth of 40 Gbps.

Benchmark results show strong multi-core performance, with a stress-ng multi-core CPU score of 103787.07 and a PassMark CPU score of 107013.97, placing it in the top tier. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, reaching 7683.86 GB/sec for cached small-block read-only operations and 389.44 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads. Single-core performance is moderate by comparison, with a stress-ng single-core score of 2121.55, representing an average tier. The processor supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX), which contribute to top-tier performance in PassMark extended instructions and encryption tests.

This instance is configured for workloads requiring high memory bandwidth and multi-threaded processing, such as database operations, static web serving, and software compilation. It achieves 172.76 million operations per second in Redis SET benchmarks and 155.47 GB/sec in static web serving throughput. For machine learning, the hardware supports medium-model LLM prompt processing at 326.29 tokens/second, though text generation speeds for larger models are average. The lack of local storage requires reliance on network-attached storage, which is a key architectural tradeoff for storage-heavy applications.
description: Amazon Web Services m8i.24xlarge is an x86_64 general-purpose instance featuring an Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor with 96 vCPUs, 48 physical cores, and 384.0 GB of DDR5 memory. Operating at 3.9 GHz with a 480 MB L3 cache, the dedicated CPU supports AVX-512 and Intel AMX extensions. The instance lacks local storage and GPUs but provides a 40 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Benchmarks indicate top-tier multi-core CPU and memory bandwidth performance, with a PassMark CPU score of 107013.97 and cached read-only memory bandwidth of 7683.86 GB/sec. It demonstrates strong capabilities in database operations, software compilation, and static web serving, processing 172.76 million Redis SET operations per second. However, single-core performance is average, and the absence of local storage requires network-attached storage solutions. This profile makes it suitable for multi-threaded enterprise workloads, web serving, and moderate machine learning inference.
